findings.reason: one clause stating either the retirement/merge or why the new rule cannot be private is all the section needs to satisfy the budget rule the plan itself enforces on other sections.
findings.text: §9 adds one public definition to `reckon/interface_counts.py` and accounts it ("grows by exactly one … deleted helpers are private and uncounted") but never says what it retires or merges, nor why nothing can be; the rule the counting module is the sole consumer of is exercised only by its own inventory test and the parity test, so a module-private name would grow public_definitions by zero, and the plan's own §5 ("the interface has a budget") is that a section adding surface must account for it

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §9 adds one function to `reckon/interface_counts.py` over the nodes `definitions` already yields, hiding the whole staged-write predicate (callee set, local-binding test, parameter hop-up, retained exceptions) behind a single small interface; it is not a spread of shallow wrappers and creates no new module.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the one duplication §9 could have made (a second AST staged-write detector beside the census's) is named with both owners: `reckon/interface_counts.py` as the authoritative runtime owner and the frozen census as the retained historical instrument, reconciled by a parity assertion that requires every function the census labels an atomic JSON replacement at the head to appear in the runtime inventory. The owner to extend is named, not forked blind.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — supplied counts public_definitions 1475, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §9 grows the public_definitions family by exactly one (the ported inventory rule on `reckon/interface_counts.py`) but names nothing it retires or merges, and does not state why nothing can be — the deleted helpers are private and therefore do not offset the growth, which §9 records without addressing why the added surface is unavoidable.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §9 cites the exact mechanisms it extends and the one it rejects, and every citation resolves: it reuses `reckon/interface_counts.py:read_trees`/`definitions` rather than adding a tree walk, lifts the call predicate from `docs/research/data/crew-pattern-review/code-depth/census.py:233 primitive_concepts` (verified nested under the JSON-encoding branch at census.py:258-274, exactly as §9 states), and rejects `reckon/clones.py:172 functions_in` on the verified ground that it returns token windows and exposes no call node. No new subsystem is added without a named search.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the "port rather than import" move is justified in the plan's own text: the census imports its sibling `candidates` unqualified at module scope (`census.py:24`, verified — `candidates.py` is a sibling), so it is not importable by a package caller, and its predicate is frozen as a measurement whose figures are compared across pinned commits. A parity assertion reconciles the two, so the runtime rule is an extension of a function whose real home moved, not a gratuitous wrapper.
